correctness.rationale: Consecutive marker gaps are exactly \(g_j=(B-1)B^j\) and each gap is unique. For at least three ones, rotation completeness imposes a geometric growth relation around a cyclic list of positive gaps and is impossible. For two ones, rotations demanding maximal preceding padding force incompatible predecessor-gap inequalities except (2,2), (2,3), (3,4), each directly exhibited. Every one-marker rotation and the all-zero factor exist arbitrarily far out. A span bound and sliding weights give Abelian complexity \(2+\lfloor\log_B nfloor\). A finite complete-factor diagnostic independently matched all formulas for 1600 base/length pairs. There are no assumptions on base primality or word recurrence.

value.rationale: Lie complexity is a natural invariant introduced to measure cyclically complete factor classes. The result classifies every such class at every factor length for all integer-base sparse automatic words, including exactly three exceptional small parameters. It establishes a sharp structural separation from their logarithmically unbounded Abelian complexity and explains the mechanism by strict geometric growth of consecutive marker gaps. This is an exact infinite classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a routine increment to an earlier result.
